question: An object, 2.0 cm in height, is placed at a distance of 6.0 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 8.0 cm, on its principal axis. Its image has a height of ________ and is ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**more than 2.0 cm, erect**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• To find the height and nature (real or virtual) of the image formed by the concave mirror, **we can use the mirror formula** 
 
• Given
 
 
• Object height (ho h_o" id="MathJax-Element-3-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">ho ho h_o hoh_o ho​) = 2.0 cm
 
• Object distance (u u" id="MathJax-Element-4-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">u u u uu u) = -6.0 cm (the negative sign is used as per the sign convention for mirrors)
 
• Focal length (f f" id="MathJax-Element-5-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">f f f ff f) = -8.0 cm (the focal length is negative for concave mirrors)
 
 
 
• **The mirror formula**
 
 
• 1/v + 1/u = 1/f ⇒ 1/v + 1/6 = 1/8
 
 
 
• On solving for v, we get, v = -24 cm.
 
• Now, m = -v/u = -(-24)/(6) ⇒ m = 4.
 
• Also, m = image height/object height
 
• Image height = m × object height.
 
 
• Image height = 4 × 2 = 8 cm.
 
 
 
• Thus, the image height has more than 2 cm and it is erect.
